correctness.rationale: For each summand, |T^n|^(1/n) is diagonal with entries exp(n^(-1) sum of n consecutive logarithmic weights). For every fixed starting coordinate k, its exponent differs from the first-prefix Cesaro logarithmic mean by at most 2B(k-1)/n; uniformly bounded diagonal entries upgrade coordinatewise convergence to strong-operator convergence. Conversely the first diagonal coefficients identify each coordinate of a weak-operator cluster limit. The vector prefix means are bounded and have successive jumps at most 2B/(n+1); their cluster set is a nonempty compact continuum. For any target continuum K in logarithmic coordinates, finite epsilon-chain polygonal tours of shrinking nets yield a bounded 1-Lipschitz curve with omega-limit K, without assuming K is path-connected. The sampled sequence c_n=gamma(log n) has that same cluster set. Its inverse Cesaro weights b_n=n c_n-(n-1)c_(n-1) telescope and have norm at most R+1, producing bounded and bounded-below positive weights. The asymptotic numerical range is the continuous image of the connected compact product K times a simplex and has the stated coordinate extrema. Independent exact rational and finite diagonal checks corroborate these algebraic steps, not the all-continua theorem.

value.rationale: The theorem exactly classifies natural WOT root-cluster geometries of finite orthogonal sums of uniformly bounded-below weighted shifts, showing a sharp change from scalar intervals with one summand to all positive planar continua with two. It addresses a whole family of objects, including non-path-connected continua, and identifies the precise information collapsed by the asymptotic numerical range. This is more informative than an isolated example or a known scalar bound, without claiming an extension to arbitrary operators.
